```python
def run_length(xs):
    """Run-length encode `xs`: split it into maximal runs of equal consecutive values and
    return a flat list [v1, c1, v2, c2, ...] where run number k consists of ck copies
    of the value vk, in order.
    """
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(xs):
        j = i
        while j <= len(xs) and xs[j] == xs[i]:
            j += 1
        out.append(xs[i])
        out.append(j - i)
        i = j
    return out
```

completion.text:
The inner loop condition is `j <= len(xs)`, which should be `j < len(xs)`. When a run extends to the end of the list, `j` reaches `len(xs)` and the loop evaluates `xs[j]`, which raises an IndexError.

Trace for `xs = [0]`:
- `i = 0`, `j = 0`. Since `0 <= 1` and `xs[0] == xs[0]`, `j` becomes 1.
- Now `j = 1`, `1 <= 1` is true, so `xs[1]` is evaluated and raises IndexError.

The same happens for any non-empty input, because the last run always reaches the end of the list. The empty list is the only input that works, since the outer loop never runs.

The docstring requires `[0, 1]` for `[0]`, but the function raises an exception.
